decisions.statement: A page and a parent are named as parts rather than as paths.
The parent a page has now is read from the index rather than handed in.
A page no page names among its parts is refused.
That refusal names the change putting a value into a property.
A page more than one page names among its parts is refused.
A page already a part of the parent named is refused.
The new parent gains the spelling the old parent used.
A parent spelling the page among its parts more than once is refused.
The mechanical changes take the value out and put the value in.
Those changes are reached through the runner rather than by an import.
The mechanical answers are gathered into one answer.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.
A parent stating no parts gains the list rather than being refused.
The list is put in by the change putting a key in rather than a value.
The list gained is written where the pages of the parent's type write that key.

definition: one page made a part of another page rather than of the page naming it now
